title: Test: Time and Verb Forms
subtitle: Answer all 10 questions to check your understanding of Time, Tense, and verb forms. You can review every answer before submitting.

questions.questionText: Look at the timetable notice: 'The morning assembly _____ at 8:15 a.m. every weekday.' Which verb form fits best?
questions.explanation: 'every weekday' describes a regular daily routine, so Present Simple ('begins') matches the singular Subject 'The morning assembly'.

questions.questionText: In the sentence 'The train to Puri leaves at 6:00 a.m. tomorrow', what real-world time does the Present Simple verb 'leaves' express?

options.text: A scheduled future event on an official timetable
An ongoing action happening right this second
A mental state that never changes

questions.explanation: Time and verb form are distinct: the Present Simple form 'leaves' is used with 'tomorrow' to communicate a fixed future timetable.

questions.questionText: Mira whispers in the library: 'Look! Arjun _____ a colourful map of Kaziranga right now.' Choose the right verb phrase.
questions.explanation: 'Look!' and 'right now' show an action in progress at the moment of speaking, requiring Present Progressive ('is drawing').

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses a state (non-progressive) verb accurately?

options.text: Rohan is knowing all the capitals of India.
This brass telescope is belonging to our science lab.
Deepa understands how solar panels produce electricity.
We are liking fresh mangoes after sports practice.

questions.explanation: Stative verbs such as 'understand', 'know', 'belong', and 'like' express states rather than physical actions, so they stay in Simple form ('understands').

questions.questionText: Read the eco-club log: 'Last Saturday, our volunteers _____ forty mango saplings along the boundary wall.' Choose the accurate verb.
questions.explanation: 'Last Saturday' names a finished past time, so Past Simple ('planted') is required rather than Present Perfect or Present Simple.

questions.questionText: Arjun points to the tidy shelves and says, 'Look, the monitor _____ all the science journals already.' Which verb completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: 'already' and the visible present result ('Look, the shelves are tidy') call for Present Perfect ('has arranged').

questions.questionText: Select the sentence that correctly communicates a planned future event for next week.

options.text: Our class will visited the planetarium next Friday.
Our class is going to visit the planetarium next Friday.
Our class visited the planetarium next Friday.
Our class has visit the planetarium next Friday.

questions.explanation: 'is going to visit' properly expresses a planned future event ('next Friday'). Option (a) wrongly puts a past verb after 'will', and (c) uses a past verb.

questions.questionText: Which time word fits naturally into the blank: 'Meera has practised Odissi dance _____ 2021.'?
questions.explanation: 'since 2021' marks the starting point of an action continuing up to now with Present Perfect ('has practised'). 'yesterday' and 'ago' belong to Past Simple.

questions.questionText: Find the grammatical error in this noticeboard slip: 'Yesterday evening, our kabaddi team has won the inter-school match.'

options.text: Plural 'team' cannot take 'has'; it should be 'have'.
Present Perfect ('has won') clashes with a definite finished past time ('Yesterday evening'); use Past Simple ('won').
There is no error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: Definite past time markers such as 'Yesterday evening' require Past Simple ('won'), not Present Perfect ('has won').

questions.questionText: Read the weather note: 'Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius, and warm air _____ upwards.' Complete the scientific truth.
questions.explanation: General scientific truths always stay in Present Simple ('rises' matching singular 'warm air').
